sites.what: Writes a SearchRecord into sign('search:index') keyed by the source layer sig; every row in it carries `sig` — the tile's own LAYER SIGNATURE, up to 4000 of them in the root record.
sites.why: Check 6, and this is the sharpest instance of it in the tree. `HistoryService.referencesOutside` (history.service.ts:4425) does NOT credit a wipe-safe pool's member NAMES but still scans its member BYTES: `for (const match of text.matchAll(/[0-9a-f]{64}/gi)) hit(...)`. `search:index` is declared `index` (pool-kinds.ts:132) so it is wipe-safe by declaration, yet one root record names the layer sig of every tile in the hive. Prune (prune.service.ts:379) then classifies those sigs as `shared`, withholds them, and reports `removed: 0` with a `shared` skip reason. The accelerator has changed what the collector keeps, which is exactly what optimize-phase.md rule 3 forbids. Records are never swept (there is deliberately no refresh path), so the pin is permanent for every sig ever indexed.
sites.smallestFix: One line in `referencesOutside`: gate the member BYTE scan on the same `creditsNames` flag that already gates the name — `if (creditsNames) await readFile(handle, 'member')`. A wipe-safe pool may be dropped at any moment, so content only IT references is already collectable by definition; scanning its bytes is the contradiction, not the protection. That single change also clears the manifests and computed:genome findings below. The per-site alternative (drop `sig` from SearchRow and re-resolve by path on click) is far more invasive and buys nothing extra.

sites.what: Persists a child's derived record under the child's real layer sig — including a record that the depth cap produced as `{ v: 1, rows: [], truncated: true }` (hive-search.ts:192) and including one the node budget cut short mid-loop.
sites.why: Check 1, in the sense that matters here: the record is keyed by a content signature but is NOT a pure function of that signature — it is a function of where the walk arrived. A sig's record can never go stale, so there is no refresh path (search-index.drone.ts:77 skips any sig that has a record), which means the first record written for a sig is its record forever. A sig reached once at depth 24 gets an empty record sealed permanently, and every future parent reads it back as a cache hit and splices in emptiness. The molecule index diagnosed exactly this shape and fixed it — molecule-index.service.ts:154-172 spells out why the depth cap must return NULL rather than an empty record, and molecule-index.drone.ts:115 refuses to write a truncated record at all. Search was left behind. It stays HONEST (readers see `truncated`) so the answer degrades rather than lies, which is why this is local and not wide.

sites.what: Read-modify-writes the whole insight catalog — participant-named tree fragments, each holding a root and the layer sigs called into it — as one document in sign('insights:catalog').

sites.what: Walks a subtree and, wherever a child location's bag head differs from the layer its parent chain names, commits the PARENT'S hint forward as the child's new head marker.
sites.why: Neither wrap-up nor break-apart: it takes a node that already carries MORE detail (a legitimately newer descendant edit) and republishes an ancestor's frozen, LESS-detailed hint over it. Its own docblock at :2805-2811 says so verbatim — 'THE INVOKER ASSERTS THE TREE… Mints real markers (truth): explicit user/repair action ONLY — never from the optimize phase, never on a schedule' — and hypergraph-molecule-lineage.md's migration table says it 'survives only as an explicit user/repair op, never as an unattended auto-repair' and 'loses ALL THREE of its callers'. It has not lost them. All three are live and all three are UNATTENDED: snapshot.queen.ts:113 calls healSubtreeBags([]) — segments [] is the WHOLE HIVE — as an automatic retry when sealSubtree fails; publish-branch.ts:226 and builds-slot.ts:183 do the same for their branch. Each is wrapped `try { … } catch { /* heal is best-effort */ }`, so a repair that rewrites every location head in the hive is silent on both success and failure. The trigger (a cold or unresolvable descendant) is exactly the condition under which the parent's hint is MOST likely to be the stale one.
sites.smallestFix: Delete the three automatic call sites (snapshot.queen.ts:113, publish-branch.ts:226, builds-slot.ts:183) and let the seal failure surface as it already does (`lastSealFailure` / `'seal-failed'`). Keep the method as a user-invoked repair verb only.

sites.what: Hydrates a machine from a committed layer, copying ONLY slots whose value is a non-empty Array; every other slot value is discarded.
sites.why: `if (Array.isArray(v) && v.length > 0) m.#slots.set(key, v.slice())` — a scalar slot silently vanishes, and output() can never write one back. That is not a hypothetical shape: core/level-roster.ts:58-60 states 'The slot may hold the array inline OR a signature pointing at a JSON array resource — both shapes are live in the wild', and life-primitive.ts:288-291 deliberately MINTS scalar slots (`layer[slot] = (await healMetaReference(...)).sig`) for scalar CHILD_SLOTS and typed payload hops, which hypergraph-molecule-lineage.md fixes as SCALAR by doctrine ('the typed payload hops (layer, resource, dependency, bee) stay SCALAR'). sites.what: Declares the field that would bind a typed reference incidence to a molecule's grammar name. Nothing in the codebase ever sets it and nothing ever reads it.
sites.why: The second half of the drift you asked about, and it is an ABSENCE rather than a bad write, which is why it is easy to miss. hypergraph-molecule-lineage.md states the incidence as `{meta:1, layer:<vertexSig>, root, relation, slot}` and says `root` IS the stable canonical grammar name — that field is the joint between the reference end ('any referenced feature can become a root') and the naming end ('a molecule is an atom one level up'). All three mint sites in the tree pass only a payload and a `relation`: presentation/tiles/artifact-content.ts:47 (`{ resource, relation }`), hypercomb-runtime/src/store.ts:882 (`{ ...payload, ...incidence }`, and every caller's incidence is `{ relation }` only), life-primitive.ts:243 (`{ ...payload, relation }`). So `moleculeAddress` / molecule-index and the meta-envelope layer are running as two independent subsystems with a declared-but-dead field between them, and the doctrine's `slot` is not in MetaEnvelope's known-field list at all (it would fall through to the alphabetical extras; `relation` is doing that job under a different name). One pattern from two ends, not yet joined.
sites.smallestFix: Have the one canonical writer set it: in Store.ensureArtifactMeta, when the incidence names a reference to a named artifact, pass `root: await moleculeAddress(name)`'s preimage (the folded canonical name). Then reconcile the doctrine's `slot` with the code's `relation` in hypergraph-molecule-lineage.md so one word means one thing. Do not add `slot` as a second field — that would make the drift permanent.

sites.what: Deletes a conversation: reads every entry in the sha256(convoId) bucket, requires each to parse as this conversation's own chat-turn/archive/goal record, then removes exactly those and the emptied bucket.

sites.what: Quarantines stray OPFS-root entries: copies each (per-file, verified) into a sign('sweep-<timestamp>') bucket inside the sign('temporary') pool, then removes the original.
sites.why: REFUTATION on check 8, with one caveat worth stating. This is a RECURSIVE removal at the OPFS root and it never calls hardDeleteVetoFor, so it fails the letter of check 8 — but it satisfies the property the check exists to protect by a different and arguably stronger route: nothing is removed until its bytes are confirmed present in the quarantine (copyFileVerified throws on a size mismatch, and the caller only removes after it returns), so a wrong classification costs a move, never data. sites.smallestFix: Change copyFileVerified's check from `written.size !== bytes.byteLength` to a SignatureService.sign comparison of the two buffers. One line, and the quarantine then proves content rather than size.

sites.what: The single door for every decoration: builds { kind, appliesTo, payload, mark?, refs? }, content-addresses it as a root resource, and appends the sig to the cell's `decorations` slot through LayerCommitter.

sites.what: Writes the raw 64-hex signature of the names map as the BYTES of a file literally named `names-master` inside the bare-word pool sign('registry').
sites.why: The member name is a caller-chosen human string, not sha256(bytes) nor any stated derivation — check 1. Two compounding consequences make this the worst site in the sweep. (a) GC BLINDNESS: packed-collect.ts:132-146 credits a pool member as a reachability root only if its NAME is a signature (`isSigName(leaf)`) or its BYTES parse as JSON (`collectSignaturesIn` returns early on a JSON.parse throw). `names-master` is neither — the name is foreign and the bytes are a bare unquoted hex string, which is not valid JSON. So the content resource the pointer names is credited by nothing, and `collect()` (packed-store.worker.ts:648) sweeps it as an orphan. Every saved name is silently gone on the next collection, and the pointer survives pointing at nothing. (b) MOLECULE POISONING: sign('registry') is a bare word, so it IS the molecule address of any tile named `registry`. A `foreign`-classified entry there permanently vetoes hardDeleteVeto AND documentSweepVeto (directory-safety.ts:90,196) at that address, so nothing can ever be cleaned there again.
sites.smallestFix: Write the pointer as a sig-named JSON member — `putPoolDoc(pool, encode({kind:'names-master', sig}), 'names-master')`. The subKey is positive proof for the sweep, the JSON body makes the target sig visible to collectSignaturesIn, and the member name becomes sha256(bytes).

sites.what: Writes a children manifest into the bare-word pool sign('manifests') under a member name that IS the parent LAYER signature, with a body of `{sig, layer}` entries inlining every child layer signature.
sites.why: Check 6, and it is not theoretical. packed-collect.ts:132-146 credits BOTH the member's name (`isSigName(leaf)` — a parent layer sig) AND every signature found in its JSON bytes (child layer sigs, and any props/visual sigs inside the inlined layer objects). Pool members are never themselves swept — `collect()` only iterates `engine.contentSigs()` and `looseSigs()`. So a manifest for a long-superseded parent pins that whole layer subtree against collection permanently. The store's own comment at line 68-72 asserts these records are 'pure derived state, safe to GC'; the collector's actual reachability rule makes that statement false in both directions — the manifest is never collected, and neither is anything it names.
sites.smallestFix: Two options, either alone closes it: (a) have `collect()` skip pools flagged derived (the derived-cache pools are already a named class) so their members neither pin nor survive; or (b) store the manifest body without raw sigs (names/props only) and key it by a non-signature derivation. (a) is smaller and also frees the pool itself.

sites.what: Eagerly creates nine BARE-WORD pool directories at the OPFS root on every boot: sign('bees'), ('dependencies'), ('clipboard'), ('threads'), ('computation'), ('manifests'), ('optimization'), ('overrides'), ('translations').

Booting mints nine directories at nine molecule addresses whether or not anything is stored in them, which is a placement decision made by the shell rather than by the reader — the same shape as the standing invariant's 'may declare, may never place', one level down. It fails no numbered check on its own; the numbered damage arrives through the four registry pointers and the two derived caches above, all of which land their foreign or pinning entries in exactly these directories. It is a known, decided debt rather than a discovery, and I am reporting it because it is the enabling condition for six of the eleven other findings.
sites.smallestFix: Open these lazily (on first read or write) rather than at init, which costs nothing and stops a boot from minting nine empty molecules. The colon migration is the real fix and is already scheduled; the lazy open is the part that can land today without a data migration.

sites.what: Writes a PUT body to a filesystem path whose DIRECTORY segments are chosen entirely by the caller's URL, with only the final segment constrained to a 64-hex sig.
sites.why: The sig check pins the BYTES and nothing about the PLACE. `resolved = resolve(cfg.contentDir, '.' + urlPath)` (relay.js:884) plus `mkdirSync(dirname(resolved), {recursive:true})` (relay.js:908) lets an authorised writer mint arbitrary directory structure inside the host's content root — including a directory named sign('bees'), sign('people') or any molecule address, and including planting a member inside a pool directory the host already serves at `/<sig>/` (the dirMatch branch, relay.js:656-676). The doctrine's own answer — `looksLikeAddressPreimage`, the address gate described in hypergraph-molecule-lineage.md — is not applied anywhere on this path. It is neither a wrap-up nor a break-apart: nothing is being gathered and nothing is being refined; a location is being asserted by a stranger.

HEADLINE: 15 of 22 write sites in this sweep conform to the root primitive. 6 are deviations, 1 is legacy-conforming.

Of the 6 deviations, 4 are ONE bug wearing four hats. `HistoryService.referencesOutside` (history.service.ts:4425) already refuses to credit a wipe-safe pool's member NAMES — the `poolCreditsMemberNames` rule, and it is correct — but it still scans that member's BYTES with an unanchored 64-hex regex. Every honest derived record in the tree names the sigs it derived from, so the byte scan re-pins exactly what the name rule just un-pinned: children manifests pin their children, search rows pin every indexed tile (4000 sigs in one root record), and the active-genome census pins the entire hive from a single file. Prune (prune.service.ts:379) then reports those sigs as `shared`, withholds them, and returns `removed: 0`. Nothing is destroyed — the failure is a permanent, silent refusal to reclaim, plus a receipt that tells the participant their tile's bytes belong to somebody else. Gating the byte scan on the same `creditsNames` flag is one line and closes all four at once; it is also safe in the correct direction, because content that only a wipe-safe pool references is already collectable by that pool's own declaration.

The other two are independent and small: search's depth cap seals an EMPTY record permanently under a real layer sig (the molecule index diagnosed and fixed this exact shape; search was left behind — two lines), and `insights:catalog` is declared a wipe-safe derived cache while holding participant-authored fragments no cold client could rebuild (one seed line; this is the only finding with a data-loss tail rather than a reclaim-loss one).
